text: Text column 0-39 for print_char at $8049 and the screen reads at $8034/$8043. Other code also uses it as a square column, for example Gordon's next square.
Text row 0-26 for print_char at $8049 and the screen reads at $8034/$8043. The row selects the start address from the row tables $0340/$0360.
Screen code that print_char at $8049 writes at column $02, row $03.
Colour that print_char at $8049 writes to the colour RAM at column $02, row $03.

Low byte of the work pointer $07/$08. unpack_graphics reads the sprite source through it. $9828 and $98d0 use it for the saved screens at $5000/$5400. It is also the sprite X position (half value) for the sprite routine $845c, a lawn shape character and a save of X.
High byte of the work pointer $07/$08. It is also the sprite Y position for the sprite routine $845c and the column of a lawn shape.

Low byte of the second work pointer $09/$0a. unpack_graphics writes the sprites through it, and $8a1e reads the status line buffer $4000/$4080 through it. It is also a save of X and the row of a lawn shape.
High byte of the second work pointer $09/$0a. It is also the width counter of a lawn shape.
Counter of the delay loops and the height of a lawn shape. The message printer $9b00 uses $0b/$0c as the pointer into the message texts.
Temporary byte: lawn shape colour, offset of the lender colours, sprite frame of an actor, high-score position and loop counter. It is the high byte of the message pointer $0b/$0c in $9b00.
Low byte of the third work pointer $0d/$0e. $8ba8 reads the lawn shape data at $8c6e through it. It is also the high-score entry offset and a temporary byte in the actor code.
High byte of the third work pointer $0d/$0e. It is also the row counter of the high-score table, a save of X and the distance temporary of the actor code.
Loop counter of the high-score table display at $7c00 and of the sound delay at $9d93.
IRQ countdown of the tune player. At 0 the tune player at $80e9 does one step and loads music_speed $11 again.
Number of IRQs for one step of the tune player. The start of a tune sets it to 3.
Low byte of the tune pointer $13/$14 of SID voice 1. Each tune entry is 2 bytes: duration and note. Note $f0 is a rest.
High byte of the tune pointer $13/$14 of SID voice 1.
Low byte of the tune pointer $15/$16 of SID voice 2. Note $f0 is a rest and $ff ends the tune.
High byte of the tune pointer $15/$16 of SID voice 2.
Steps left of the current note of voice 1. At 0 the tune player reads the next entry.
Steps left of the current note of voice 2. At 0 the tune player reads the next entry.
Not 0 while a tune plays. The IRQ clears it at the $ff end mark of voice 2. $8236 waits for 0, and $8259 starts the game tune when it is 0.
Joystick bits from $864a, inverted so that 1 means pressed: bit 0 up, bit 1 down, bit 2 left, bit 3 right, bit 4 fire.
Current player, 1 or 2.
Index of the joystick register from $dc00: 1 reads port 1, 0 reads port 2. With 2 sticks the player change toggles it.
Number of joysticks, 1 or 2, from the setup screen.
Base of the current player's variables $20-$27 for the copy loops with X = 1 to 8 ($8a1e loads them, $9922 saves them). The code does not use $1f itself.
Lender of the mower: 1 JIM, 2 TOM, 3 ALF. It goes up when a neighbour catches Gordon. At 4 the game of the player ends.
Current lawn number, from 1. After lawn 16 the lawn shapes repeat and the game runs at maximum speed.
Low byte of the grass counter $22/$23: squares left to mow. A new lawn sets it to $0348 (840). When both bytes are 0 the lawn is done.
High byte of the grass counter $22/$23.
Column of the end of the DOG LOYALTY bar on screen row 22 ($1e full). $959a lowers it. At $0f the bar is empty and Rover does not obey the fire button.
Column of the end of the DOG TOLERANCE bar on screen row 23 ($1e full). $9624 lowers it. At $0f the bar is empty and Rover chases Gordon.
Column of the end of the MOWER OVERLOAD bar on screen row 24 ($10 empty). Mowing raises it. At $1f the mower overheats. $9234 lowers it again.
Number of players, 1 or 2, from the setup screen.
Countdown of the message on screen row 21. The IRQ decrements it and clears the row at 0. $9b00 prints a new message only when it is 0.
Current move direction of Gordon: 1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, 0 stopped. It also selects the sprite frames of the mower.
Direction in which an obstacle or the lawn edge stops Gordon. A joystick move in this direction does nothing.
Speed of Gordon, 0-7. It goes up while the stick stays in the same direction, and goes to 0 at a stop. The step delay is $46 minus 8 times this value.
Screen column of Gordon's square.
Screen row of Gordon's square.
Sprite X position of Gordon, half value (the sprite routine $845c doubles it).
Sprite Y position of Gordon.
Steps left to the next square. A move to a new square sets 4. At 0 the game tests the grass counter and the next square.
The start of a lawn clears this byte. No code reads it.
Animation frame 0-2 of the mower sprite. Each step adds 1.
Walk frame 0-2 of Gordon (sprite 0). place_mower_and_gordon adds it to the frame of the direction. Each step adds 1.
Main loop countdown to the next step of Gordon. $91f5 loads it again with $46 minus 8 times gordon_speed $32.
Frequency high byte of the sound effects on SID voice 3: mowing, barking, the bonus count and the high-score entry.
Not 0 while the mowing sound plays. $9327 lowers sfx_pitch $3c each time and stops the sound at 0.
1 while the mower is overheated or after Rover bites Gordon. Gordon cannot move, and the mower sprite flashes. The overload cool-down clears it.
1 while the mower is overheated or after Rover bites Gordon. Gordon cannot move, and sprite 0 (Gordon) changes colour. The overload cool-down clears it.
Main loop countdown of the mower cool-down. At 0 $9234 lowers the overload bar by one step and loads $c0 again.
Main loop countdown of the task at $9327: keys, Rover's bark and the mower sounds. It runs every 16 loops.
Low byte of the screen pointer $48/$49: start of the row in cursor_row $03. With $d4 added to the high byte it points to the colour RAM.
High byte of the screen pointer $48/$49.
Main loop count between two actor moves. The lawn number sets it: 12 minus half of (lawn number AND 15), 4 after lawn 16.
X position of the target of the current actor: Gordon, Rover or the neighbour.
Y position of the target of the current actor.
X position of the current actor divided by 4, for the compare with the target.
Y position of the current actor divided by 4, for the compare with the target.
Move direction of the current actor: bit 0 set moves up, clear moves down. Bit 1 set moves left, clear moves right.
Facing of the current actor, 0 or 1 (bit 0 of actor_dir inverted). It selects the sprite frames.
Number of active actors: 2 (Rover and the neighbour), 3 when the gardener comes.
Main loop countdown to the next actor move. $951a loads it again from actor_speed $50.
$ff when an obstacle stops the vertical move of the current actor. $9525 then sets the sprite frame and clears it.
Last random value from the raster line. It gives the direction of an actor that wanders (mode 3).
Countdown while the fire button is down. At 0 the DOG LOYALTY bar drops one step and loyalty_rate $60 loads it again.
Random pause between two barks of Rover, from the raster line.
3 after Rover has bitten Gordon, else 0. The overload cool-down clears it.
Not 0 when the music is off. C= and M toggles it. The tune player then keeps the gates closed.
Reload of loyalty_timer $5c. The lawn number sets it: 6 minus the lawn number divided by 4, 2 after lawn 16.
Reload of loyalty_timer $5c. On lawns 1-16 it is always 6, because speed_by_lawn_number uses LDX where the code needs A. After lawn 16 it is 2.
Low bytes of the start addresses of the 27 screen rows from $0400. $800d builds it.
High bytes of the start addresses of the 27 screen rows from $0400. $800d builds it.
Screen field of the entry lawn digit on the setup screen (row 13, column 13). F1 steps it from 1 to 8.
Screen field of the players digit on the setup screen (row 13, column 26). F3 steps it from 1 to 2.
Screen field of the three initials of the high-score entry (row 13, columns 27-29). $9f19 steps each letter with the joystick.
Screen field of the sticks digit on the setup screen (row 13, column 38). F5 steps it from 1 to 2.
The byte before message_row. The clear loop of the IRQ indexes it with X = 40 down to 1.
Screen row 21: the line of the messages of $9b00.
Score field on screen row 22. The code indexes it with X = 1 to 7: the seven digits are at $0790-$0796.
Screen field of the lender name (JIM, TOM or ALF) on status row 23, columns 33-35. $8a1e writes it.
X position (half value) of each actor, X = 1 to 4. Actor 1 is Rover, 2 the neighbour, 3 the gardener. Actor X uses sprite X+1.
X position of Rover (actor 1).
X position of the neighbour (actor 2).
Y position of each actor, X = 1 to 4.
Y position of Rover (actor 1).
Y position of the neighbour (actor 2).
Move countdown of each actor. At 0 the actor moves, and the speed table at $8ff2 loads it again.
Mode of each actor: 0 chases Gordon, 1 runs away from Rover, 2 chases the neighbour, 3 wanders at random.
Mode of Rover: 3 wanders, 2 chases the neighbour (fire button), 0 chases Gordon (DOG TOLERANCE empty).
Mode of the neighbour: 0 chases Gordon, 1 runs away from Rover.
Mode of the gardener: 0 chases Gordon, 1 runs away from Rover.
Countdown of each wandering actor. At 0 it takes a new random direction and a new random count from the raster line.
Animation frame 0-3 of each actor. Frame 3 shows frame 1 again.
Moves left until the next animation frame of each actor (3).
Character set of the game, 2 KB. unpack_graphics copies it from $6400. $d018 = $18 selects it.
Sprite data of the game: 64 sprites of 64 bytes, pointers $c0-$ff. unpack_graphics copies them from $6c00.
Status lines of player 1: 120 bytes for screen rows 22-24. $8995 fills it from $89a6, $9922 saves the screen rows into it, $8a1e prints it.
Status lines of player 2: 120 bytes for screen rows 22-24, as status_p1.
Base for the shift of the high-score table at $9e25: $4bf6+Y is the entry before $4c00+Y.
High-score table, indexed with Y = 1 to 50. It holds 5 entries of 10 bytes at $4c01-$4c32: 7 score digits and 3 initials as screen codes. $9dcc fills it from $9e43.
The byte before player1_state. The clear loop at $8667 indexes it with X = 32 down to 1 and clears $4f00-$4f1f.
Saved variables $20-$27 of player 1 at $4f01-$4f08, indexed with X = 1 to 8: $4f01 mower lender, $4f02 lawn number, $4f03/$4f04 grass counter.
Saved variables $20-$27 of player 2 at $4f11-$4f18, as player1_state.
Saved screen rows 0-21 of player 1 (880 bytes). $9828 fills it, and $98d0 draws it again at the next turn of the player.
Saved screen rows 0-21 of player 2 (880 bytes), as saved_screen_p1.
Saved colour RAM of rows 0-21 of player 1 (880 bytes), 8 pages after saved_screen_p1.
Saved colour RAM of rows 0-21 of player 2 (880 bytes), 8 pages after saved_screen_p2.
Tune 1: $8236 starts it with voice 1 at $6000 and voice 2 at $6200, and waits until it ends.
Tune 2, voice 1: $825d starts it from $6032 when no tune plays. Voice 1 has no end marker. Voice 2 ends the tune.
Last entry: a rest of 240 ticks. $ff fill bytes follow.
Notes of SID voice 2, read through the pointer $15/$16 at $8143. Same format as voice 1. Note $ff ends the tune: the player clears the tune flag $1a.
The pair at $622e is the end of tune 1 (note $ff). It is also the start address of tune 2, voice 2, which $825d sets.
End of tune 2 (note $ff).
The same values are in the game at $8ed9-$8eed.
The 128 characters of the game. unpack_graphics copies $6400-$67ff to the charset at $2000-$23ff.
The first message starts at $67f9 ("UNDEFIN"), but the last character of the charset replaces its first 7 bytes.
Leftover: the address table of the error messages, 29 words from $23f9 to $2606 in the memory of the assembler. Words $0000 have no message.
Leftover: powers of ten 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000 as a split table (5 low bytes, then 5 high bytes).
Leftover: 6502 code of the assembler at its own addresses $265f-$27ff. It calls the KERNAL routines CHKIN, CHRIN, CHKOUT, CHROUT, CLRCHN, CLOSE, STOP and GETIN.
64 sprites of 64 bytes. unpack_graphics copies them to $3000-$3fff, sprite pointers $c0-$ff.

Entry of the program. Unpacks the charset and the sprites, then starts the game init at $81ff.
unpack_graphics: charset to $2000, sprites to $3000
Builds the tables of the row start addresses of the screen: low bytes at $0340, high bytes at $0360. There are 27 rows of 40 bytes from $0400.
Next row: 40 bytes on
Gets the screen address of row $03 into $48/$49 and the column $02 into Y. Changes X.
Reads the screen code at column $02, row $03 into A.
Writes the screen code $04 and the colour $05 at column $02, row $03. It writes nothing for the columns 40-167 ($28-$a7).

Sets the IRQ vector $0314 to irq_handler and the NMI vector $0318 to nmi_handler. Clears the message timer $2f. Starts the raster interrupt at line 0. Stops the tune ($1a = 0), sets the tune tempo $10/$11 to 3 and the SID volume to 15. Then copies the status texts (JSR $8995).
X is not used
Raster interrupt on
Writes the $d011 value to the voice 3 control register
Raster line bit 8 = 0
Tune off
NMI handler: RTI only. The RESTORE key does nothing.

IRQ handler. An interrupt that is not the raster interrupt goes to the KERNAL at $ea31. On the raster interrupt (line 0, each frame), when the tune flag $1a is not 0, it counts down the tempo counter $10. When it gets to 0, it reloads it from $11 and does one tune step: the message timer and the two voices of the tune. Then it goes to the KERNAL at $ea31.
Acknowledges the raster interrupt
Tune flag: 0 = no tune
Message timer $2f
Timer at 0: clears the message row 21 ($0748-$076f)
Voice 1: counts down the duration $17. At 0, the pointer $13/$14 moves on by 2 and the next note starts. A note is 2 bytes: the duration in tune steps, and the note number. Note $f0 is a rest.

Note number to frequency
Music flag $5f: not 0 = music off, no gate
Sawtooth, gate on
Voice 2: counts down the duration $19. At 0, the pointer $15/$16 moves on by 2 and the next note starts. Note $f0 is a rest. Note $ff ends the tune: the tune flag $1a becomes 0.
$ff: end of the tune
Low bytes of the SID frequency of the notes 0-60, one semitone for each note. Note 0 is $0218: C-1 with the NTSC clock. The tunes use the notes 19-57.
One byte between the two tables. The tune player does not read it.
High bytes of the SID frequency of the notes 0-60.

Game init after the cold start. Builds the screen row tables, initialises the high-score table (JSR $9dcc) and installs the interrupts. Sets the SID envelopes. Sets player 1 ($1c), lender 1 for both players ($4f01, $4f11), joystick port 1 ($1d) and music on ($5f = 0). Then starts the attract sequence at $9fa0.
Voices 1 and 2: attack 0, decay 9
Voice 3: attack 3, decay 9
No filter, sustain 0, release 0
$1d = 1: joystick port 1
Plays the jingle and waits until it ends. Voice 1 reads from $6000, voice 2 from $6200, with tempo 3. The first notes are at $6002 and $6202.
The IRQ clears $1a at the end of the tune
When no tune plays ($1a = 0), starts the main tune again: voice 1 from $6032, voice 2 from $622e, with tempo 3. The first notes are at $6034 and $6230. Changes A.

Start of a game from the setup screen. Copies the status texts, selects player 1 and joystick port 1, and sets music on. Clears the state of both players, then gives each player lender 1 ($4f01, $4f11) and the entry lawn $21 ($4f02, $4f12). Then starts the turn of player 1.
Entry lawn from the setup screen

Title screen. Clears the screen, sets a black border and background and the charset at $2000. Writes the credit texts column by column: rows 1, 8, 10, 12 and 22. Fills row 6 with the grass character $58. Plays the jingle and waits, then the mower mows the logo.

Gordon (sprite 0, frames $c0-$c4) pushes the mower (sprite 1, frame $c5) from left to right along row 6. Each column of grass becomes mown grass ($59). Four columns behind the mower, the letters of the logo appear. Fire jumps to the setup screen.

Draws a block of 2x2 characters with the colour $05. The screen codes $04, $04+1, $04+2, $04+3 go to the top left, bottom left, top right and bottom right of column $02, row $03. On exit, $02 and $03 are 1 more, and $04 is 3 more.

Else it fills rows 0-20 with grass (char $73), sets the grass counter to 840 and draws the layout of the lawn. Then it starts play at $8f30.

Decreases the grass counter $22/$23 (squares left to mow) by 1. The game calls it for each mown square and for each square that is not grass.

Decreases the grass counter by 2 for each row. Changes $09 and $0a.

Records: $7c column,row,length (vertical strip), $7e column,row,length (horizontal strip), $ff end. Other bytes: char,column,row,width,height,colour (rectangle).

Colour 9 makes a bed of rings: each inner ring is 1 square smaller on each side and uses the next colour. Ring squares are not counted again.
Increments the layout pointer $0d/$0e and reads the byte there. Output: A = the byte, Y = 0.
Layouts of the 16 lawns, read by $8ba8. Each lawn ends with $ff. This first $ff is the mark before lawn 1.
Lawn 1.
Lawn 2.
Lawn 3.
Lawn 4.
Lawn 5.
Lawn 6.
Lawn 7.
Char $76 without bit 7. The square at column 13, row 4 is already subtracted by the record before.
Lawn 8.
Lawn 9.
Lawn 10.
Lawn 11.
Lawn 12.
Lawn 13.
Lawn 14. The developer's source fragment at $63c0 holds bytes $8ed9-$8eed of this lawn.
Lawn 15.
Lawn 16.
Extra end mark after lawn 16. The lawn index is never 17.
It sets Gordon's start state ($30 = 8, right, mower at $35/$36 = $51/$cd, $33/$34 = $12/$14), places the sprites ($8f8e) and jumps to $9066.
Clears $d000-$d00f, the sprite positions.
Gordon is behind the mower: the tables at $8fd3 and $8fdc give his offset from the mower. Changes $07 and $08.
Mower sprite frame for each direction 0-8 (only 1, 2, 4 and 8 are used).
Gordon's first sprite frame for each direction. The code adds the step $39.
X offset of Gordon from the mower for each direction (signed).
Y offset of Gordon from the mower for each direction (signed). Entry 8 is the byte at $8fe4.
Start values of actors 1-4, index X = 1-4 (index 0 is the byte before). X positions to $1f00+X.
Y positions of actors 1-4 to $1f10+X.
Start values of actors 1-4 to $1f30+X. $9381 compares this value with 2.
Reload values of the step counter $1f20+X of actors 1-4. $938f reads them.
Then it sets $57 and $5c to 2 and the speed values $50, $58 and $60 from the lawn number $21. After lawn 16 it uses the maximum speed.
Second part of the actor setup at $8ff6. It turns on sprites 0-3 and sets the speeds of the lawn from the lawn number $21.
Multicolour for sprites 0, 1, 3 and 4.
$57 = 2: two actors move. $5c: the countdown of the DOG LOYALTY decrease.
(Lawn number - 1) AND $f0 is not 0 after lawn 16.
Maximum speed after lawn 16: $60 = 2 and the actor period 4.
Lawns 1-16. LDX does not change A, so A is 0 here and $94bd returns 0. Thus the loyalty period $60 is always 6.
$50 = 12 - (lawn AND $0f) / 2. Lawn 16 gives 12, as lawn 1 does.
$50: the period of the actor moves. $58: its countdown.
The byte before actor_colours.
Sprite colour of actors 1-4 (sprites 2-5): black dog, yellow neighbour, dark grey gardener, light red actor 4.

Starts the play of a lawn. It stops Gordon and clears the flags $3d, $3e and $5e. The DOG LOYALTY and DOG TOLERANCE columns $2a and $2b go to $1e (full). The MOWER OVERLOAD column $2c goes to $10 (empty). Then it sets up the actors at $8ff6, shows message 3 ('COME BACK HERE WITH MY LAWNMOWER!!') and goes into the main loop.
$30: the direction of Gordon. 0 stops him.
The main loop: the delay, the timer of Gordon, the mower cooling, the sound and key tick, and the actor timer.
Waits 128 DEY loops. Then it calls $8259.

Moves Gordon one step. First it runs the dog command at $95c0. Nothing moves while the mower is overheated ($3e = 1). With steps left in $37, it moves the position $35/$36 in direction $30. At 0 steps, Gordon is on a square.
Direction $30 bits: 0 up (Y-2), 1 down (Y+2), 2 left (X-1), 3 right (X+1).
Counts the step in $37 and steps the walk frame $39 through 0, 1 and 2.
Places sprites 0 and 1 at $8f8e.
Gordon is on a square. When the grass counter $22/$23 is 0, the lawn is complete: JMP $99c5.
Puts the next square in direction $30 into $02/$03 and $07/$08.
Mows the square at column $02, row $03. The square $07/$08 becomes the square $33/$34 of Gordon. Then it tests the square after it.
Writes the character that $920a gives.
Characters $7c-$7f block the way.
Column -1 or 40 is off the screen.
Row -1 or 21 is off the lawn.
The way is blocked. $31 keeps the blocked direction, the speed $32 goes to 0 and Gordon stops ($30 = 0).
Copies the square $33/$34 of Gordon to $02/$03 (column, row). Then it moves that square in direction $30 at $9156.
Moves the square $02/$03 one square in direction $30: 1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right. Direction 0 changes nothing.
Reads the character at column $02, row $03 with $8043. A holds the character, and $48/$49 with Y point to it.
Reads the joystick of the player into $1b. When the stick holds the direction $30, the speed $32 goes up and Gordon moves on.
Speed 7 is the maximum.
Starts 4 steps ($37) to the square $07/$08.
Takes a new direction from the stick: bit 0 up, bit 1 down, bit 2 left, bit 3 right. No direction stops Gordon.
When the new direction is the blocked direction $31, Gordon stays. Else the speed $32 goes to 0 and Gordon turns on the square $33/$34.
Counts down $3a. At 0 it loads $3a with $45 - 8 x the speed $32 and moves Gordon at $909d.
The carry is clear, so SBC subtracts 1 more.

Mows the character in A and returns the new character in A. Mown grass $7b and mown flowers $77 do not change. Flowers $76 add 2 steps to MOWER OVERLOAD and start the gardener. They give $77. Other characters give $7b.
Grass: $8b10 decreases the grass counter $22/$23. Then it adds one MOWER OVERLOAD step and adds the lawn number to the score.
$7b: the mown grass character.
The byte before scale_chars.

The characters of a scale cell, from empty to full: $20 (space), $2a, $29, $28, $26, $25, $24, $23 and $22 (full). A step up writes scale_chars,x after a match at scale_chars-1,x. A step down writes scale_chars-2,x.
Every 192 calls ($3f), removes one step from the MOWER OVERLOAD scale on row 24 at column $2c. When the column $2c goes down to $19, an overheated mower runs again.
Row 24: the MOWER OVERLOAD scale.
The cell is empty. The column $2c moves one to the left, but not to $0f.
At column $19: $3e = 0, voice 3 noise starts, sprite 0 is yellow and $5e = 0.

Adds one step to the MOWER OVERLOAD scale on row 24 at column $2c. It keeps A, X, Y, $02, $03 and $48/$49. When the dog does not attack ($1f31 is not 2), it starts the mower noise on voice 3 ($3d, $3c = $ff).
The cell is full. The column $2c moves one to the right.
Column $1f: the mower overheats. Voice 3 plays a triangle, $3e = 1 and message 9 shows ('OH RATS!.. THE MOWER HAS OVERHEATED!').
Adds 1 to the score digit X, Y times. The digits are on the screen at $078f+X, and X = 7 is the last digit. A digit after '9' becomes '0' and adds 1 to the digit on its left. It keeps X.
Adds the lawn number $21 to the score. It keeps X and Y.

Every 16 calls ($40), it checks the keys and updates voice 3. When the dog attacks ($1f31 = 2), $9698 makes the sound. Else an overheated mower flashes sprite 0. The mower noise falls in pitch until $3c is 0.
The pause and music keys.
The mower is overheated ($3e = 1). Sprite 0 changes colour, the colour sets the pitch of voice 3, and the speed $32 stays 0.
Moves the actors $57 down to 1. An actor moves when its countdown $1f20,x gets to 0. An actor in mode 2 moves on each call.

Moves actor X one step. It loads its countdown from $8ff1,x and steps its frame $1f50,x (0-3) every 3 calls. At the end of each frame cycle it calls $9659 (DOG TOLERANCE). Then it moves the actor and places its sprite.
$9434 gives the direction $55 and $96c7 tests the collisions. $0c gets the frame $e4 + 3 x $56 + the frame.
Bit 0 of $55 set: Y - 2. Else Y + 2.
When $94c2 finds the place blocked, the old Y stays and $5a is $ff.
Bit 1 of $55 set: X - 1. Else X + 1.
Stores the position, sets the sprite frame at $9525 and places sprite X + 1 with $845c.

Sets the direction bits $55 and $56 of actor X. Mode 3 takes a random direction at $957b. Mode 0 goes to Gordon, mode 2 goes to the neighbour (actor 2) and mode 1 goes away from the dog (actor 1). $51/$52 get the position of the target.
Gordon: $35 and the Y of sprite 1.
Compares the positions divided by 4. Bit 0 of $55: the actor is not above the target (move up). Bit 1: it is not left of it (move left).
Mode 1 inverts both bits: the actor goes away from the dog.
$56 = 1 when bit 0 is 0 (the actor moves down).
Divides A by 4 with two RORs and a clear carry.

Tests the place $07/$08 of actor X. It returns A = 0 when the actor can go there, else A = $ff. It keeps X. The limits are Y = $2c or $ce and X = $08 or $a4. Column = (X - 8) / 4, row = (Y - $28) / 8. Characters $73, $7b and $77 are free. Flowers $76 are free for actors 2 and 4, but not for the dog and the gardener.
Counts down $58. At 0 it loads $58 from the period $50 and moves the actors at $9374.
Sets the sprite pointer of actor X (sprite X + 1). A blocked actor ($5a) or a Y distance below 8 to the target gets a side frame. Mode 3 or a large Y distance keeps the frame $0c from $938f.
Side frame: $ea + the frame, + 3 when the actor moves left.
The frames of the dog (actor 1) are $0c higher.
Random walk of actor X in mode 3. When the count $1f40,x gets to 0, it takes a new random value $5b. $55 = the value AND 3, and $56 = 1 when bit 0 is 0.
Reads the raster line $d012 as the random value. The next count is the value AND $3f.
Removes one step from the DOG LOYALTY scale on row 22 at column $2a. Column $0f is an empty scale. When a cell becomes empty, the column $2a moves one to the left. The bonus at $9a80 also calls it.
Reads the joystick. With bit 4 (fire) or bit 6 of $1b and DOG LOYALTY left, the dog attacks the neighbour. Else the dog walks at random and the neighbour and the gardener chase Gordon.
The dog takes mode 3 (random). With an empty DOG TOLERANCE ($2b = $0f) and $5e = 0, it takes mode 0 (chase Gordon).
Actors 2 and 3 take mode 0. Then $9665 tests if the neighbour is near the dog.
Fire: with DOG LOYALTY left, message 4 shows ('ROVER.. KILL!! GO ON, BOY! SIEZE! KILL!'). The dog takes mode 2 and actors 2 and 3 take mode 1 (flee). Every $60 calls, DOG LOYALTY goes down one step.
Starts the gardener: $57 = 3 actors, message 7 ('OI! OFF MY FLOWERS, YOU LUNATIC!') and sprite 4 on. It returns A = $77, the mown flower character. It keeps X.

Removes one step from the DOG TOLERANCE scale on row 23 at column $2b. Column $0f is an empty scale. When the scale becomes empty, the dog takes mode 0 and message 8 shows ('OH DEAR... THE DOG LOOKS ANNOYED...!').
Calls $9624 and keeps X and Y. $938f calls it at the end of each frame cycle of an actor.
Tests the distance of the dog (actor 1) and the neighbour (actor 2). With an X difference from -16 to 15 and a Y difference from -24 to 23, the neighbour takes mode 1 (flee).
Sound of the dog attack on voice 3. While $3c is not 0, a sawtooth rises in 8 steps. Then it waits a random time $5d and starts again.
Reads the raster line $d012. The pause $5d is the value AND $1f.
Tests actor X against its target $51/$52 and against Gordon $35/$36. The X difference must be -7 to 5 and the Y difference -8 to 7.
The actor is at its target. Mode 0 goes to $9718. Modes 1 and 3 go on to the test against Gordon.
Mode 2, the dog at the neighbour: adds 1 to the score and shows message 5 ('AAARGH!  LAY OFF, YOU BEASTLY HOUND!').
The dog (actor 1) goes to $974a. The other actors go to $97ae.
Tests actor X against Gordon: an X difference from -5 to 4 and a Y difference from -7 to 6.
Gordon touches the dog. One time only ($5e = 3), it fills MOWER OVERLOAD, empties DOG TOLERANCE and stops the mower.
Fills row 24 with full cells ($22) from column $2c to $1e.
This exit goes to $9783 past the code at $977a. Thus message 10 never shows.
Code that nothing reaches: it clears $2f and shows message 10 ('DAMNATION!!  I'VE HIT THE DOG!').
Empties DOG TOLERANCE: spaces on row 23 from column $10 to $1e, and $2b = $0f.
Voice 3 plays a triangle and the mower stops ($3e = 1).
An actor catches Gordon. $9b00 shows a message only when $2f is 0, so it clears $2f and shows message 6 ('GIMME THAT MOWER!!'). Then the actor walks to the right with Gordon until its X is $c0.
Places the sprite of the actor, then sprite 1 with pointer $d6 at 8 to the right of it.
The code from $97ae continues here. It shows sprite 1 with pointer $d6 at the neighbour position and moves the neighbour to the right.
Waits 3 x 256 calls of $8259.
Moves the neighbour one pixel to the right.
Repeats until the X position is $c0.
Scrolls out the lawn and keeps it for the player.
The colours go 8 pages higher, to $5800 or $5c00. The routine turns off the sprites and voice 3. Input: the current player $1c.
Row 0.
$0c counts the 40 steps of the row.
Reads the character at column 0 of the row.
Adding $d4 to the high byte gives the colour RAM address.
The colour goes 8 pages after the character.
Moves the characters of the row one column to the left.
Puts a space in column 39.
Moves the colours of the row one column to the left.
Waits 96 calls of $8259 after each step.
Stops after row 21.
With 1 player, the player borrows the next mower. After the third mower, the game is over.
$20 is the number of the mower: 1 JIM, 2 TOM, 3 ALF.
Loads the player state and draws the status rows.
Shows the lender message of the new mower.
Then it continues at $8f30. $8ac2 also jumps here when the grass counter $22/$23 is not 0.
The screen code for $8049.
The colour for $8049.
Stops after row 21.
Then it resets the three scales and copies the status rows 22 to 24 of the screen to $4000 (player 1) or $4080 (player 2).
Row 24 (MOWER OVERLOAD) gets spaces, empty cells.
Reads row 22 to row 24: 120 characters from $0770.
When player 2 loses the third mower, the game is over. Else the other player gets the turn: $8a1e loads the state and $8672 starts the lawn.
Resets the stack.
Changes the port: 1 to 0, 0 to 1.
The next mower of this player.
Player 1 to 2, player 2 to 1.
Loads the state of the new player and draws the status rows.
"WELL DONE!" flashes in all colours with a falling tone. The bonus follows when the DOG LOYALTY scale is not empty.
Changes the text to a screen code.
32 rounds of 256 colour steps.
Gives the colour to the 10 characters of "WELL DONE!".
The frequency of voice 3 follows the colour counter.
Sawtooth with the gate on.
$2a is the column of the last cell of the DOG LOYALTY scale in row 22. $0f: the scale is empty.
Starts the next lawn: it increments the lawn number $21, saves and loads the player state, resets the stack and jumps to $8ac2.
Resets the stack. fidelity_bonus ends with a JMP to next_lawn, not with RTS.
It plays a rising tone and calls $959a to make the scale one step shorter. When the scale is empty, it jumps to next_lawn and does not return.
Adds Y to score digit 6, the tens.
Triangle with the gate on.
Makes the DOG LOYALTY scale one step shorter.
Does not return with RTS. next_lawn resets the stack.
"WELL DONE!   PREPARE FOR MORE MOWING!": 37 characters for lawn_complete. The code ANDs each byte with #$3f to get the screen code.
"CANINE FIDELITY BONUS": 21 characters for fidelity_bonus.
Plays 6 rising sawtooth sweeps on voice 3. At each step, background colour 2 ($d023) changes. At the end, voice 3 is off.
When the message timer $2f is not 0, it shows nothing. It sets $2f to $30. The interrupt clears row 21 when $2f gets to 0.
$0b/$0c points to the first message.
Skips one message: it finds the $ff at its end.
Row 21 of the screen.
Message 0: " JIM WON'T MIND IF I BORROW HIS MOWER...". $8743 shows messages 0 to 2 for the mower $20.
Message 1: "     I'LL JUST NIP AND BORROW TOM'S!    ".
Message 2: "   GOOD OLD ALF! HE'S A DECENT CHAP!    ".
Message 3: "   COME BACK HERE WITH MY LAWNMOWER!!   ".
Message 4: "ROVER.. KILL!! GO ON, BOY! SIEZE! KILL! ".
Message 5: "  AAARGH!  LAY OFF, YOU BEASTLY HOUND!  ".
Message 6: "           GIMME THAT MOWER!!           ". The code at $97ae shows it.
Message 7: "    OI! OFF MY FLOWERS, YOU LUNATIC!    ".
Message 8: "  OH DEAR... THE DOG LOOKS ANNOYED...!  ".
Message 9: "  OH RATS!.. THE MOWER HAS OVERHEATED!  ".
Message 10: "     DAMNATION!!  I'VE HIT THE DOG!      ". It has 41 characters. print_message shows the first 40. No call gives X = 10.
Message 10. Only the dead code at $977a prints it, so the game never shows it. It is 41 bytes, one more than the row.
Each command waits until the key is released. Uses $028d and the key code $c5.
Bit 1: the C= key.
Key M.
$40: no key.
Key P.
Waits for any key.
Then it clears columns 13 to 29 of these rows, row by row. It continues at hiscore_check.
$8049 gives Y = the column that it wrote.
Voice 3 off.
Plays a falling sawtooth tone on voice 3: the frequency high byte goes from $40 to 1. Uses $3c and $0f.
"GAME OVER": 9 characters for game_over.
8 colours: blue, red, purple, green, cyan, yellow, white, black. game_over and $7c0e read them.
Copies the initial high-score table (50 bytes) to $4c01-$4c32 as screen codes. The cold start at $81ff calls it.
A score that is higher than an entry goes into the table. A score that is equal does not.
Loads the state of player $1c and draws the score in row 22.
$0d: offset of the entry in the table.
The score digits are at $0790-$0796.
Joystick port 1 again.
Shows the high-score screen and continues the attract loop.
Moves the entries below the new place one entry down. The last entry is lost.
The last entry needs no move.
init_hiscores uses $9e42, the high byte of this operand, as the base of its table.
The initial high-score table: "0000000JCM", "0000000NOT", "0000000TEG", "0000000ZAP", "0000000POW". init_hiscores reads it from initial_hiscores_m1 + 1.
Writes the score into the entry and shows "PLAYER ONE" or "PLAYER TWO" in row 10 and "ENTER YOUR INITIALS:  AAA" in row 13.
$0c: offset of the initials in the table.
"PLAYER ONE": 10 characters. $7cab also reads it.
"PLAYER TWO": 10 characters. $7cab also reads it.
"ENTER YOUR INITIALS:  AAA": 25 characters. The three A characters are the start values of the initials at $0623-$0625.
The current letter is cyan. Player 2 with 2 sticks uses port 2. After the third letter, it continues at hiscore_next_player.
Reads the joystick into $1b.
Left: the letter before. '@' goes to 'Z'.
Right: the next letter. 'Z' goes to '@'.
6 rising triangle sweeps.
The stored letter is white.
The cold start at $81ff jumps here. $8658 leaves the loop to the setup screen when the fire button is down.
hiscore_done enters the loop here.
Clears the lawn area and writes "MEGA  MOWER  MANIACS" from $7cca in row 2 in yellow. Then it jumps to $7c00, which shows the table.
$7c00 returns to the caller of show_hiscore_screen.
11 bytes of $ff.
27 bytes of $00.
The bytes $4c,$4d,$4f,$4e,$4e: the ASCII text "LMONN".
